messages:
Alex (oncall): Morning handoff — I'm primary for 06:00-14:00. Devon is secondary. Heads up: infra scheduled autoscaler maintenance 09:00-09:30 UTC, expect increased queueing on hosted pool. Leaving a short checklist and links below.

Alex (oncall): Coverage gaps: non-prod burst was causing noisy neighbor issues last night, I've disabled non-prod bursts (did that at 2076543220). If you need to re-enable, @Priya please coordinate. :white_check_mark:

Priya: Ack, thanks. Can we also clamp the max batch size for high-latency routes temporarily?

Alex (oncall): Yes — lowered max batch to 8 on /text-gen-high via routing override. Command I used: `rctl route update /text-gen-high --max-batch=8 --comment "autoclamp during autoscaler maintenance"`

incident-bot: Incident #1723 created: high p99 latency for hosted text generation (detected by latency-alerts). Severity: S2.

Jorge: Seeing p99 jump to ~1.8s and a small rise in 502/503s. KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 68%. Queue length also climbed on batcher-02.

Alex (oncall): Runbook -> https://redwood.runbooks.com/api-high-latency (pinned). Quick triage steps: check batcher queue, check worker pod restarts, verify KV cache availability. Common quick fixes listed below.

Alex (oncall): Quick commands:
```
# check batcher queue
kubectl -n inference exec -it svc/batcher -- curl localhost:9000/metrics | grep batch_queue_length
# list worker pods
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=worker -o wide
```

Molly: If batcher backlog is the cause and worker count is healthy, consider routing to smaller model variant as a graceful degrade. In Console -> Routing -> Override, or via CLI:
```
rctl route set /text-gen-high --model redwood/small-v1 --duration 15m --reason "mitigation: reduce latency"
```

Devon: If pods hit OOM/killed, check `kubectl describe pod` and `dmesg` on node. We have a quick restart script if node-level memory is transient: `infra-restart-worker <node-id>` (ops-only). Also check node memory pressure metric on infra dashboard.

Kai: Customer impact: looks limited to lower-tier tenants on hosted region us-west-2. Recommend status update: "degraded performance affecting some hosted customers; engineering investigating." I'll draft the support blurb and ping support@redwood.

Alex (oncall): Also check KV cache cluster (redis-1 replica lag) -> Redis console link: https://console.redwoodinfra/metrics/redis-1. If replica lag > 200ms, failover or reduce read pressure by routing to model variants that don't hit heavy prefix cache.

Priya: If the autoscaler maintenance at 09:00 causes a temporary shortage, we should enable burst capacity on Dedicated (if on call customer is affected) — but that's manual and requires billing/ops approval. Leaving note for handoff to night team.

Alex (oncall): Handoff checklist I left in the runbook doc: https://redwood.runbooks.com/oncall/shift-checklist — includes links: dashboards, runbooks, infra-ops playbook. Pinning main dashboards: latency, error-rate, batcher-queues, kv-cache.

Jorge: Reproduced higher latency on canary: payload sizes were bigger than usual, some tokenization edgecases spiking KV misses. I'll add a short prompt size filter to the ingress rule as mitigation.

Devon: Secondary ack. I'll stay on for escalation if needed. If you leave early @Alex, drop a note and hand the bridge to me.

Priya: FYI I'm out at 12:45 today, Devon covers the overlap.

incident-bot: Incident #1723 resolved at 2076543270 — automated closure after latency returned to baseline for 10m.

Alex (oncall): Final notes: root cause likely transient cache replica lag + heavier-than-normal payloads during autoscaler maintenance window. Postmortem checklist: capture request traces for spike window, evaluate autoscaler windows, consider pre-warming burst capacity for future maint windows. Leaving breadcrumbs in the thread and in the runbook. :spiral_note_pad:
